standard_prerequisites.name: A localization of a finite type algebra at a prime is integral over the localization of the finite type algebra after an integral base change, so dimensions agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the localized finite type algebra over the new base is one dimensional and Noetherian, which is the setting for the integral closure.

standard_prerequisites.name: Krull-Akizuki: the integral closure of a one dimensional Noetherian domain in a finite extension of its fraction field is Noetherian
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes each of the finitely many integral closures of the quotients Noetherian.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a one dimensional local ring the residue field extension in a finite extension of the fraction field is finite
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the finiteness of the residue field extensions asserted in the statement.

core_obligations: Write the larger discrete valuation ring as the localization at a prime of a finite type algebra over the smaller one, so that after base change to the integral extension the result is a finite type, hence Noetherian, algebra which is integral over the original one (proof lines 35937-35941).

Conclude that the localization at the prime is integral over the given ring and compute that its dimension is one, using that dimension is preserved under integral extensions (proof lines 35941-35945).

List the finitely many minimal primes of that one dimensional Noetherian ring, and for each take the integral closure of the corresponding quotient in the fraction field of the reduced base change, obtaining finitely many Noetherian one dimensional rings by Krull-Akizuki (proof lines 35946-35952).

Record that the residue field extensions in these integral closures are finite, and identify the product of the finitely many closures with the integral closure of the given ring in the reduced base change, which gives Noetherianity, surjectivity of the spectrum map and the finiteness of the residue field extensions (proof lines 35952-35958).
proof_roadmap: Present the larger ring as a localization of a finite type algebra and base change to the integral extension (proof lines 35937-35941).
Use integrality to see that the dimension is one and list the finitely many minimal primes (proof lines 35941-35946).
Apply Krull-Akizuki to each quotient and conclude Noetherianity, surjectivity and finiteness of the residue extensions (proof lines 35946-35958).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an extension of discrete valuation rings with the larger ring essentially of finite type over the smaller one, and an algebraic extension of the fraction field whose integral closure in the base is required to be Noetherian; it concludes that the integral closure in the reduced base change is Noetherian, that the induced map of spectra is surjective and that the residue field extensions are finitely generated (statement lines 35925-35935). The proof presents the larger ring as a localization of a finite type algebra, base changes along the integral extension to obtain a one dimensional Noetherian ring integral over the original one, lists its finitely many minimal primes, and applies Krull-Akizuki to the finitely many resulting one dimensional domains to get Noetherianity, with the finiteness of the residue extensions coming from the one dimensional case (proof lines 35937-35958). The reduction to finitely many one dimensional Noetherian domains is what makes all three conclusions come out of the same computation. The counted span refers three times to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
